solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 13-across

clue.text: Transform oneself into a boon companion

parts.note: to transform something is to alter it
the ego is the self, one's own identity

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to remake themselves into a jolly drinking partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, so a bosom friend inseparable from one.

clue.text: Poetic village, in colour

explanation.surface: A village known from verse is described by its hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet Auburn is the village of Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village; it is also a reddish-brown hair shade.

clue.text: Make-up paints she used for stage people

indicators.note: make-up signals the letters of paints she are made up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actress uses greasepaint for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' looks like cosmetics after 'paints', but it is the signal to rearrange PAINTS SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespians are actors, after Thespis, the first actor of Greek drama.

clue.text: Come up again about a pay increase

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a rise is a pay increase in British usage

explanation.surface: A pay increase is raised once more at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rise' is the British word for what Americans call a raise in pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearise is to rise or emerge a second time.

clue.text: For whom tramps played a waiting game

definitions.text: For whom tramps played a waiting game

parts.words: For whom tramps played a waiting game
parts.note: in Beckett's play two tramps, Vladimir and Estragon, wait for a man who never comes

explanation.surface: Vagrants idly wait around for somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' is literal: the tramps are characters in Beckett's play Waiting for ..., and the man they await gives the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Godot is the absent figure in Beckett's play, awaited by its two vagrant heroes.

clue.text: Get money on the favourite? Seems a little dear

parts.note: to pop something is to pawn it, raising cash on it
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A punter puts cash on the favourite, which looks a bit pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' looks like 'expensive' after the betting talk, but here it means a darling; 'Seems' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is an affectionate term for a small child or sweetheart, a darling.

clue.text: Visual contraction in stone

indicators.note: the contraction piece goes in the stone word

parts.note: opal is a precious stone
a tic is an involuntary muscular contraction

explanation.surface: A spasm seen in a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contraction' looks like a shortened word but is a muscle twitch, TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight or the eye.

clue.text: Was this light a guide for Fanny?

definitions.text: Was this light a guide for Fanny?

parts.words: Was this light a guide for Fanny?
parts.note: the film Fanny by Gaslight suggests the small gas flame that is always kept burning, and which also names a guide such as a ship's navigator

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which lamp lit the way for a girl named Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny by Gaslight is a British novel and film; a gas appliance's small standing flame shares its name with a guide who steers ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a guide, and a pilot light is a small standing gas flame.

clue.text: The Hampshire river affair is taken to court

definitions.text: The Hampshire river affair is taken to court

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, a county in southern England, famed for trout
a case is an affair or matter

explanation.surface: A dispute over a county river ends up before the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; its River Test is famous for fly fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit brought to settle a legal principle for later disputes.

clue.text: Musical state

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance show about a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodgers and Hammerstein's 1943 stage show shares its name with a US state in the South Central region.

clue.text: Some life in our alley?

parts.note: the saying that life is not all fun and games is turned round: a skittle alley in a pub is where the pleasures it names really are found

explanation.surface: A neighbour asks whether there is any liveliness in their back street.
explanation.walkthrough: A skittle alley is a lane in a British pub for skittles, a form of ninepins; the clue plays on the proverb that life is not all of this pair of pleasures.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pleasure and fun, drink and pub games, which is life in a skittle alley.

clue.text: Salesman isn't commonly on the ball, of course

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
ain't is the common or colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A sloppy-speaking salesman is naturally sharp and alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ball' looks like the idiom for alert; it is literal: a ball, of course, is something one may give a fresh coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To put new paint on a ball, as is done with worn balls, is to give it a second coat.

clue.text: Hermit-like skinhead has a vinegary exterior

indicators.note: the vinegary word forms an exterior round the other piece, so it encloses it

parts.note: acetic means relating to vinegar, which is acetic acid
read as skin's head, the first letter of skin

explanation.surface: A sour-faced recluse with a shaven head is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a shaven youth but gives the head of 'skin', S, which goes inside ACETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic lives in austere self-denial, as a hermit does.

clue.text: Borrow unusually novel rag-book

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of novel rag are set in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, from the front of rag-book

explanation.surface: Someone borrows an odd new cloth picture book for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow, the English writer, wrote the novel of this name (1851); 'Borrow' with 'book' points to his work, and the anagram of NOVEL RAG gives it, 'book' tying the definition to the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavengro is George Borrow's best-known book, a semi-autobiographical novel about Gypsy life.

clue.text: What a gardener did with flowers, say, was horrible

indicators.note: say signals the words are heard spoken aloud, giving a word with another spelling

parts.words: What a gardener did with flowers
parts.note: a gardener grew some flowers, cultivated a few

explanation.surface: A gardener's work with flowers turned out ghastly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grew some' spoken sounds like the word for horrible; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means causing horror or disgust, ghastly.

clue.text: They display their forte in a great many high places

indicators.note: the musical letter is put in the word for a great many

parts.note: lots means a great many
f is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud

explanation.surface: Performers show off their talents in lofty venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forte' looks like a strength or talent; it is the musical term, abbreviated F.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofts are upper rooms or galleries high up in a building or barn.

clue.text: Tray-upsetting Hoffman boy

parts.note: Heinrich Hoffmann's German book of cautionary verses, Struwwelpeter, tells of a badly behaved boy who comes to grief

explanation.surface: A clumsy lad named Hoffman knocks over a tray.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoffman is not the boy's surname: Heinrich Hoffmann wrote Struwwelpeter, cautionary tales of naughty children, one of them cruel Frederick.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick is the misbehaving boy of one of Hoffmann's verses in Struwwelpeter.

clue.text: A stringed 26 seems to prohibit support of the wood section

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
a joist is a supporting beam of timber

explanation.surface: A string player appears to be against backing the woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is a player of an instrument; 'wood section' looks like the woodwind of an orchestra but is a timber section, the beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist plays the banjo, a stringed instrument, so is a string player.

clue.text: A tailpiece is the point of the orbit

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a piece added at the tail of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a coda is what a planetary path is for.
explanation.definitionFit: An apsis is either extreme point of an elliptical orbit, nearest to or farthest from the centre.

clue.text: Up for the Cup ? Yes, for this one

definitions.text: Up for the Cup ? Yes, for this one

parts.words: Up for the Cup ? Yes, for this one
parts.note: the football phrase for travelling to a Cup Final is read as being mounted on a horse, ready for a parting drink served to a rider

explanation.surface: A football fan asks if someone is going to the Cup Final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for the Cup' is British slang for fans travelling to the FA Cup Final; here the cup is the drink handed to a rider already in the saddle before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a drink given to a rider mounted and about to leave, foot in the stirrup.

clue.text: Girl with the goods on her taken by surprise

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
wares are goods for sale

explanation.surface: A woman is caught off guard while carrying her merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the goods on her' places WARES after UNA; 'taken' is a link, as in 'taken unawares'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unawares means without warning, catching someone off guard.

clue.text: Equip players for battle with something on the sleeve

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons for battle
a band is a group of musical players

explanation.surface: Troops are kitted out for war with an insignia on the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for battle' belongs with 'Equip' in the surface; ARM alone is the piece, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An armband is a strip of cloth worn round the upper arm on a sleeve, as a badge.

clue.text: Whipped-up lather for a horse's neck

indicators.note: whipped-up signals the letters of lather are whisked into a new order

explanation.surface: Foamy soap is meant for a horse's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped-up' suits a horse's sweaty lather but signals an anagram of LATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a rope headstall fitted round a horse's head and neck for leading it.

clue.text: Parliament had the ear of this man in 1738

definitions.text: Parliament had the ear of this man in 1738

parts.words: Parliament had the ear of this man in 1738
parts.note: a ship's captain showed MPs the ear he said Spanish coastguards had cut off, leading to the War of the Ear in 1739

explanation.surface: A history note says MPs listened to a certain man in 1738.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had the ear of' looks like 'listened to'; literally, the captain brought his severed ear before the Commons in 1738.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Jenkins was the mariner whose cut-off ear gave its name to an Anglo-Spanish war.

clue.text: Airy sort of passages in Palestrina's allegro

indicators.note: the word is found in the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A music critic praises the light passages in a fast movement by Palestrina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passages' looks musical, after Palestrina, but means the airways of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal passages are the air ducts behind the nose.

clue.text: Greek valley artist's mode of painting

parts.note: Tempe is a famous valley in Thessaly, Greece
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's technique is named after a Greek beauty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk, a method used before oils.

clue.text: Transport of silver not going up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a silver vehicle isn't climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India.

clue.text: Tan suit minstrel changed into-a guitar-player?

indicators.note: the letters of tan suit minstrel are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A minstrel in a brown suit turns into a guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist is one example of a musician who plays an instrument, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Puts one pound out for flowers

indicators.note: out signals these letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone spends a quid on a bunch of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring-flowering bulbs with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Its stars guided reprisal air raiders in wartime

definitions.text: Its stars guided reprisal air raiders in wartime

parts.words: Its stars guided reprisal air raiders in wartime
parts.note: the 1942 German revenge raids on historic English cities were said to pick targets starred in a famous tourist guidebook series

explanation.surface: A wartime memory of bombers steered by the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like navigation by the night sky; they are the guidebook's stars rating sights, and the 1942 raids on Bath, York and others took the guide's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Baedeker guidebooks rate sights with stars, and the Baedeker raids hit cities rated highly in them.
